title: ICICI Life Names Sidharatha Mishra MD and CEO as Anup Bagchi Departs for HDFC Bank
excerpt: The insurer's board appointed Mishra for a five-year term effective October 14, subject to IRDAI approval, after Bagchi resigned to take over as HDFC Bank chief on October 27.
body:
• ICICI Prudential Life Insurance has appointed Sidharatha Mishra as managing director and CEO for a five-year term, effective October 14, 2026, subject to IRDAI approval.
  • Mishra, currently head of digital channels, NRI and partnerships at ICICI Bank, will first join as chief operating officer on October 6.
  • Anup Bagchi steps down on October 13 after writing to the board on October 1, and takes over as MD and CEO of HDFC Bank on October 27 following RBI approval.
  • The twin appointments reshuffle leadership at two of India's largest private financial institutions within weeks.

ICICI Prudential Life Insurance has named Sidharatha Mishra as its next managing director and chief executive officer, completing a leadership transition set in motion by Anup Bagchi's departure for HDFC Bank. The insurer's board approved Mishra's appointment as additional director, MD and CEO for five years at a meeting on Friday, with the term effective October 14, 2026, or the date of approval by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India, whichever is later.

The announcement, made in an exchange filing, follows Bagchi's resignation as MD and CEO with effect from October 13. A day earlier, HDFC Bank had disclosed that the Reserve Bank of India approved Bagchi's appointment as its MD and CEO for a three-year term beginning October 27, 2026, under Section 35B of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

A staggered handover

The transition has been choreographed with unusual precision. Mishra will first join ICICI Prudential Life as chief operating officer on October 6, a week before Bagchi's exit, giving the incoming chief a running start on the insurer's operations. His CEO tenure can begin the day after Bagchi leaves at the earliest, depending on when IRDAI approval lands.

Bagchi wrote to the ICICI Life board on October 1 to say he was leaving to take up a career opportunity outside the company, according to Outlook Business, which reviewed the filing. He told the board he would support the transition and ensure a smooth handover of duties, thanking the board, the ICICI Group, the management team and stakeholders for their trust. The board, in turn, credited him with steering ICICI Life into a "resilient franchise" during his tenure.

Following his exit, Bagchi will no longer count as key managerial personnel for determining the materiality of events and disclosures to stock exchanges under Regulation 30(5) of the SEBI listing rules, the filing noted.

A bank insider takes the insurer's helm

Mishra arrives as an ICICI Group veteran with more than 25 years across retail, corporate and wholesale banking. At ICICI Bank he heads digital channels and partnerships, the voice channel, customer service, and the non-resident Indian (NRI) and international financial institution groups — portfolios that sit at the intersection of the bank's technology push and its global client franchise.

His LinkedIn profile describes a focus on innovation, customer experience and building high-performing teams, according to the Asia Insurance Post. He holds a bachelor's degree in science and a postgraduate diploma in management specialising in finance from Utkal University in Bhubaneswar. The insurer disclosed that he is not related to any of its directors and is not debarred by SEBI or any other authority from holding the office.

Bagchi's record and what changes at HDFC Bank

Bagchi's move to HDFC Bank is the headline story for India's banking sector. Associated with the ICICI Group since 1992, he served as executive director at ICICI Bank from 2017 to 2023 — overseeing retail, business and rural banking before wholesale banking — led ICICI Securities as CEO, and took charge of ICICI Prudential Life in June 2023. Under his leadership the insurer crossed Rs 10,000 crore in annualised premium equivalent for the first time in FY25, with APE rising 15% to Rs 10,407 crore and profit after tax climbing nearly 40% to Rs 1,189 crore, according to the bank's own filing.

At HDFC Bank, he succeeds Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose three-year term ends on October 26 after he decided not to seek reappointment. The RBI communicated its approval of Bagchi's appointment and remuneration on October 1, and HDFC Bank's board approved his induction as an additional director with effect from October 2, subject to shareholder approval.

What to watch

Investors will now track two timelines: the IRDAI's sign-off on Mishra's appointment and his early priorities at ICICI Prudential Life, where digital distribution and protection-led growth remain the battlegrounds with HDFC Life and SBI Life. The sharper question may be at HDFC Bank, where Bagchi takes the helm of India's largest private lender at a moment of intense competition for deposits and digital banking talent. For NRI customers, who form a meaningful slice of ICICI Bank's deposit base, Mishra's background running the bank's NRI and digital businesses suggests continuity in the cross-border products they rely on.
